0f0cb93db5: <0>Tomorrow</0> nobody knows the price, but one thing is certain: GNR gets harder to mine. Every block pays 5 GNR to all miners together, so the more computers join, the less each one gets; and every 2,100,000 blocks (about four years) the reward halves. With 28 computers one of them mines about 250 GNR a day; with 100,000 computers the same machine mines 0.07 GNR a day. That is the idea behind the calculator's first price model: <1>if a day of mining stays worth what it is worth today, one GNR becomes worth as many times more as it takes more work</1>. Someone who gets 1,000 GNR for $3 today would need about 3,500 times as much work for them among 100,000 miners.
